did: A cards essay can now carry a spoken card: an exchange in two voices, a question and an answer, each either a line Kokoro says or a take of yours from home, so your introduction plays your own voice and the DB essay can have you ask and Kokoro answer. It is drawn in the essays' two-bubble template, the one speaking lit, in the cards' dark look, with your takes played whole and captioned from what home heard; code lays every frame and nothing is cut. Home hands the takes over beside the essay and waits until each is transcribed; a take home couldn't hear stops the render, and Studio's Renders says why. I rendered a sample end to end on mock takes.

calls.title: Where your voice enters the general video essay
options: a spoken card in the cards cut list, drawn by the essays' two-bubble template
a new burn-in that redraws the bubbles
an essay kind of its own
cut the takes by hand in a free editor
calls.why: The video is made by code from your own takes on home, so no editor can stand in, and the two-bubble template already draws a conversation; only the gap was built.
calls.undo: Remove the spoken role from the cards cut list and its stage; only the sample uses it.

calls.title: A take home couldn't hear stops the whole render
options: play a silence in its place, as the Rust essay does
calls.why: A showcase should not quietly drop one of your answers; the Rust essay's silence was made for weekly work.
calls.undo: Have the spoken card play a silence for an unheard take instead (C812).

calls.title: An answer over about a minute is shown in the captions only
options: write it out up to 170 words, captions alone past that
always write it out and refuse an answer that overflows
calls.why: 170 words just fits the frame; a longer take would otherwise stop the render after the questions were already voiced.

calls.title: Each exchange is one turn of each voice
options: one of Kokoro's lines and one of your takes, in either order
an inverted flag on the card
allow two turns in the same voice
calls.why: The template is two voices; naming each turn's voice holds both your introduction and the DB essay with no flag.
calls.undo: Drop the one-of-each rule in the spoken card's checks (C817).

left: Screen zoom in cards essays (the phone's photographed screens zoomed to their parts): held at the coordinator's word as the run winds down; the agreed design is on #3311.
The spoken card's opt-in to the new characters (Mochi and the tin birds): W7's #3322 adds it after this merge.
Home's half of spoken cards (handing over takes, waiting for transcription) is server#1052, and home's render pin must move past #3315 before a spoken card renders there.
The essay's ten-minute length check can't count your takes before they're read.
